citations.narrative:
The outdoor enclosures housing two black-and-white ruffed lemurs, six ring-tailed lemurs, two red-ruffed lemurs, and six
cotton-topped tamarin, and two red-handed tamarin do not have a sufficient perimeter fence. The facility does not have a
complete perimeter fence at least 6 feet tall fully around these enclosures. There is a six foot fence on the east side of the
property facing the road, but this fence does not attach to anything. To the south there did not appear to be any fence and
to the north there was a four foot pasture fence that is in disrepair.
An insufficient perimeter fence can allow unwanted animals or people to enter the facility and potentially harm the animals
within. The perimeter fence must be constructed so that it protects nonhuman primates by restricting unauthorized
humans, and animals the size of dogs, skunks, and raccoons from going through it or under it and having contact with the
nonhuman primates. It must be of sufficient height (at least six feet high) to keep unwanted species out. It must be of
sufficient distance (at least three feet) from the outside wall or fence of the primary enclosure to prevent physical contact
between animals inside the enclosure and outside the perimeter fence.
To be corrected by September 29, 2026.

The facility did not have a perimeter fence for the one giant anteater, one capybara, two red kangaroo, twenty one straw-
colored fruit bats, and two grey foxes housed in outdoor enclosures. The facility does not have a complete perimeter
fence at least 6 feet tall fully around these enclosures. There is a six foot fence on the east side of the property facing the
road, but this fence does not attach to anything. To the south there did not appear to be any fence and to the north there
was a four foot pasture fence that is in disrepair.
Perimeter fences act as a secondary containment measure for the animals housed therein and restrict outside persons or
animals from entering. Without a perimeter fence, animals may escape or persons or other animals may interact with the
regulated animals.
All outdoor housing facilities (i.e., facilities not entirely indoors) must be enclosed by a perimeter fence that is of sufficient
height to keep animals and unauthorized persons out. Fences less than 6 feet high for other animals must be approved in
writing by the Administrator. The fence must be constructed so that it protects the animals in the facility by restricting
animals and unauthorized persons from going through it or under it and having contact with the animals in the facility, and
so that it can function as a secondary containment system for the animals in the facility. It must be of sufficient distance
from the outside of the primary enclosure to prevent physical contact between animals inside the enclosure and animals
or persons outside the perimeter fence. Such fences less than 3 feet in distance from the primary enclosure must be
approved in writing by the Administrator.
To be corrected by September 29, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
